core.title: Name the plan artifact's object of control as a kebab-case noun phrase
core.given: A planner is authoring or revising a plan artifact
core.when: the plan artifact's object of control (the controlled subject of the plan artifact) is set or changed
core.then: Synthesize the specific thing being controlled or manipulated as a kebab-case noun phrase.
prefer: A specific noun phrase in kebab-case naming the controlled subject.
avoid: Verbs, actions or full sentences as the object of control instead of a noun phrase.
core.why: A plan artifact is scoped to one object of control, and the plan artifact's statement template consumes it, so it must be a specific, consistently formatted noun phrase.
evidence: Each plan artifact's object-of-control value matches a kebab-case pattern and reads as a noun phrase naming a specific controlled subject.
verification: Check every plan artifact's object-of-control value against the pattern: a kebab-case noun phrase (lowercase words joined by single hyphens).
Coverage split: the kebab-case form is mechanically checkable; whether the value reads as a noun phrase naming the specific controlled subject is not mechanically decidable and is judged.

Scope: the check applies when an object of control is set or changed; edits to other parts of a plan artifact (e.g. its acceptance wording) and work that creates or changes no plan artifact are out of scope.

values: plan artifact's object-of-control field added or modified
object of control not a noun phrase

fires: Planner authors a new plan artifact and must state what it controls or manipulates.
Planner edits an existing plan artifact's object of control.
doesNotFire: Planner edits only a plan artifact's acceptance wording without touching its object of control.
Work on code or tests that does not create or change a plan artifact.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's local name for the plan artifact role; every core reference to 'plan artifact' (title, given, when, why, evidence, activation terms, fires, doesNotFire) instantiates to this name in the realization.

bunOnly.text: Term id: object_of_control — defined as 'the controlled subject of the DESIRED OUTCOME.'
bunOnly.reason: The term id is this realization's machine identifier for the concept (like a detector or finding id); the neutral definition 'the controlled subject of the plan artifact' lives in the core's when and verification, without the id.

Literal trigger terms: 'DESIRED OUTCOME' is the profile-supplied local artifact name and 'object_of_control' is the realization's machine field-id spelling; the core keeps only the neutral terms ('plan artifact' via the profile, 'object of control').

bunOnly.text: values: ["DESIRED OUTCOME added", "DESIRED OUTCOME object_of_control field added or modified"]
bunOnly.reason: The exact change-event strings name the concrete artifact kind and the concrete field id; they are what the stack's diff-level observer matches on, so the exact wording stays with the realization.

neutralityNotes: The only non-neutral token in the rule was the artifact name 'DESIRED OUTCOME', replaced everywhere (title, given, when, why, evidence, activation values, fires, doesNotFire) by the plan-artifact role, instantiated from roles.plan_artifact.name; no other profile key is needed because bun.json states no path, suffix, URN or tooling for this rule. 'kebab-case' was kept: it is a text-level value format, not a stack, runtime or language construct, and generalizing it (e.g. to 'the stack's casing') would weaken the obligation. The machine field/term id 'object_of_control' and the exact trigger, finding and change-event strings are realization identifiers (like detector ids) and are bunOnly; the core says 'object of control'. fires and doesNotFire are not numbered items; they were neutralized by the same artifact-name substitution. bun.json declares no severity or disposition, so verification records none.
